acceptanceAdditions.storeIntegration: SUPERSEDES the former schemaRangeRouting and writeMigrationFlow entries, both recorded from T-010 plan rounds 25-28 and both naming machinery the owner's Revision-38 scope cut DELETED (SnapshotSchemaRangeError, SnapshotWriteMigrationRequiredError, migrateManifestForWriting, rebuildForDowngrade, recoverPendingPins). None of those symbols exist; left in place they would have pointed T-011 at an API surface that was never built. The shipped contract is the derived-cache one: (1) The store is VERSION-SCOPED. T-011 addresses only <stateDir>/store-v<SCHEMA_VERSION>/ and must never open, migrate, repair, or stat another version's directory - that is what makes T-010 AC 5's 'existing files byte-identical after the refusal' true by construction rather than by care. There is no reverse migration and no schema-range error to route on. (2) T-011 acquires the port-lock authority FIRST and passes it as the WriteAuthority seam into startWriter, which asserts authority before it sweeps staging - a process that already lost the lock must not begin a sweep, because the fixed staging names it would clear may by then belong to its successor. The authority T-011 passes MUST be one constructed by createLatchingWriteAuthority: the type is branded, so a raw PortLock no longer satisfies the seam, and AC 8's assert-immediately-before-every-mutation guarantee cannot be bypassed by supplying a hand-rolled object at the public boundary. (3) startWriter returns status first-run | usable | not-usable. On not-usable it has ALREADY attempted a reset; T-011 logs resetError.reason for observability and MUST NOT branch on it (every reason has the same disposition), then rebuilds from ccusage. On first-run it rebuilds. On usable it resumes, treating unreferencedGenerations as ordinary GC input rather than damage. (4) The reset outcome is NOT assumed to be success. T-011 must inspect three fields, each a hard stop with a different meaning: reset.failed means the reset itself could not complete and the store is in an UNKNOWN state - do not rebuild, surface it, and a retry is permitted only from a fresh startWriter; reset.stoppedAtManifest means the manifest unlink failed, and because that unlink is the atomic visibility boundary the store is INTACT and still readable, so T-011 surfaces the failure and does NOT proceed to rebuild; reset.stoppedOnAuthorityLoss means the lock is gone - stop, do not retry, another process owns the store. Only a reset with none of the three set may be followed by a rebuild. (5) The store's dominance check is ADVISORY (read-then-rename); T-011 supplies the live manifest and accepts that a writer held past its check regresses to stale-but-complete, self-corrected by the next dominating publish. (6) collectGarbage no longer takes a manifest parameter - it reads and validates the live one itself - so T-011 must handle two non-fatal outcomes it cannot cause and must not treat as success: noManifest means the store has no readable manifest and NOTHING was collected (the correct response is to rebuild, not to retry GC), and abortedOnManifestChange means a concurrent publish moved the manifest mid-sweep and the sweep stopped early by design (the correct response is to leave the residue for the next sweep, since re-running immediately races the same publish). Integration tests required: authority acquired before startWriter is called and rejected when not latching; a not-usable store rebuilds and converges (a second startWriter reports first-run, never not-usable again); each of failed, stoppedAtManifest and stoppedOnAuthorityLoss halts the bootstrap with zero rebuild; both noManifest and abortedOnManifestChange are surfaced rather than counted as a clean sweep; another version's directory is never addressed by any seam call. Recorded 2026-08-03 from the T-010 code review, replacing entries invalidated by the scope cut. Round-3 amendment: rewritten via a dot-notation path after the round-2 write stored the whole object as a JSON STRING, and extended with the reset.failed, branded-authority, and GC-outcome clauses the first version omitted.
acceptanceAdditions.storeIntegrationCorrections: Two errors in storeIntegration above, caught by codex at T-010 code review round 4, corrected here rather than by silently editing the text they appear in. (1) The factory is exported as createWriteAuthority, NOT createLatchingWriteAuthority - a T-011 following the original wording would fail to import it. The class is LatchingWriteAuthority; the factory that builds one is createWriteAuthority(inner, onLost). (2) The convergence assertion was wrong about which status to expect: after a reset the store is empty, so classification is first-run; once the rebuild PUBLISHES a snapshot, the next startWriter returns usable. Assert both phases separately - first-run immediately after the reset and before the rebuild, usable after it - rather than expecting first-run twice, which would pass only if the rebuild silently wrote nothing. (3) Also strengthened since that text was written: the runtime brand is a module-private WeakSet, not instanceof, because Object.create(LatchingWriteAuthority.prototype) with an own no-op assertHeld passes instanceof while holding no latch at all. T-011 must pass an authority the factory built; nothing else is accepted, and a forged one is refused at every entry point with AuthorityHandlerContractError. (4) The store's read seam gained openRead (O_NOFOLLOW) and readAll, and no longer reads store artifacts by pathname; any adapter T-011 supplies must implement both, refuse a final-component symlink with an ELOOP-coded error, and route every failure through classifyFsError. Recorded 2026-08-03.

description:
## Why this ticket exists

v0.2 turns spendbar from a run-on-demand CLI (v0.1, complete on branch `v0.1-ts-port`, shipped as 0.1.0) into the service/view architecture: **`spendbar service run` is the headless daemon and SOLE snapshot writer**; menubar (v0.3) and MCP/CLI (T-013) are views/readers. The shape was fixed by four rounds of external Codex review of `product-architecture-2026-07-30.md` ("Service & data layer" + "Launcher + LaunchAgent" sections): round 2 forced minimal durable `install|start|stop` + launcher INTO v0.2 (a short-lived CLI/MCP invocation must hand indexing to something that survives its exit); round 3 added socket path rules and the honest headless definition; round 4 finalized stop/start sequencing. The zero-lifecycle-scripts rule (npm 12 / pnpm 10 block dependency scripts) is why the launcher design exists at all — nothing can be set up at install time.

**T-008's verdict is recorded** (`docs/v0.2-prototype-findings.md`) and it rejected the primitive this ticket originally specified. Both lockfile candidates are disproven — reproduced, not argued: a lock file outlives its owner and must be reclaimed, and Node exposes no atomic compare-and-delete, no inode-conditional replace, no flock; `rename()` orders takeovers but cannot revoke the previous winner. The adopted primitive is a **kernel-owned loopback port bind**: death releases it, nothing is ever reclaimed. Everything below that touches locking, staleness, or socket credentials is specified against that verdict (this rewrite resolves ISS-030's T-011 entry and folds ISS-041 and ISS-026 where they name this ticket).

## Scope — in

1. **`service run`**: headless daemon; the **single-instance guard IS the port bind** — a continuously held listener on `127.0.0.1:<allocated port>`. No PID file, no lock file, no staleness logic, no takeover, no inode revalidation: that state does not exist in this design. Concretely, per the findings doc (§3.4–§3.5):
   - **Write-once port allocation.** First run binds an ephemeral port and publishes it via `link()` (never clobbers); losers of a first-run storm close their listener and bid for the winner's port, where the kernel exclusion rule finally applies. The publication winner's ephemeral listener IS the lock listener (adopted with no close-and-rebind gap; an adversarial bind in that window must get `EADDRINUSE`). **No automatic re-allocation, ever** (it recreates the split-owner race); rotation is an offline act.
   - The allocation file is coordination state validated **fail-closed** (owner uid, mode exactly 0600 masked at 0o7777, type, encoding, any-non-privileged-port range) and **never repaired in place**. Coordination state IS fsynced — candidate bytes, and the directory after `link()` — through a short-write-safe loop; a lost allocation is not recomputable, it is a second singleton. (Snapshots are a different durability boundary — see the T-010 dependency.)
   - **`EADDRINUSE` is diagnosed, not assumed.** A domain-separated challenge–response over the 0600 token (protocol id + purpose + allocation id + the challenger's 256-bit, length-framed nonce in the MAC) classifies the holder. Our own live instance → report "already running", exit cleanly, never publish. Foreign or unidentifiable holder → **named error, refuse to start** — indeterminate must never collapse into either answer — with the allocation file byte-identical afterwards. A loopback TCP port is machine-wide, not uid-scoped: another local user holding it is an **accepted boundary**; the failure is refuse-to-start, **never two writers**.
   - **Honest exclusion contract.** Exclusion holds exactly while the listener stays bound; the kernel frees the port before JavaScript sees the `close` event, so a successor can enter while the former holder still runs. An unrequested close raises a positive lock-loss witness. Three requirements on THIS ticket (they are not properties of the primitive): (1) every publish path calls `assertHeld()` immediately before its atomic commit with no awaits in between; (2) `onLost` must terminate the process or irreversibly disable publishing — returning quietly is not an allowed handler; (3) the suite carries a mutant whose publish path omits (1) and it MUST fail.
   - Hosts the refresh state machine; publishes only through T-010's atomic publication protocol.
2. **Refresh state machine**: ONE execution queue; every job (fast tick, full, wake, manual, shutdown flush) carries a generation number; coalescing; **publish-if-current as the queue's internal discipline** — no superseded generation becomes current within the service. Cross-process freshness rests on the single-writer topology (every publisher goes through this service holding the port) plus T-010's advisory dominance check; the worst case under unexpected lock loss is a stale-but-complete snapshot, self-corrected by the next dominating publish — never a torn one. This ticket builds the queue/state machine skeleton; T-012 plugs the two tiers into it.
3. **Control socket**: Unix-domain socket at `/tmp/spendbar-<uid>/svc.sock` — **keyed on uid, not username**, so path length is bounded by construction (canonical form 34 bytes at a 3-digit uid, 41 at a 10-digit uid; both well inside 104). Request IDs; bounded message sizes; timeouts; protocol version negotiation; operations = status / refresh / stop / progress. Path rules, all downstream of the measured truncation finding — macOS **silently truncates** `sun_path` past 104 bytes: `listen()` succeeds, `server.address()` reports the full untruncated path (it lies), and a different path sharing the first 104 bytes connects to the same server:
   - **Reject before `listen` is ever called** on `Buffer.byteLength(canonicalPath) > 104`, measured on the **canonical** form (`/tmp` → `/private/tmp` adds 8 bytes; the canonical string is what the kernel sees). A post-listen `lstat` of the requested path is defence in depth only and can never be the primary check — a planted socket inode at the requested path makes it pass while the true endpoint is the truncated prefix.
   - Trusted root canonicalized first, then **no symlinks strictly below it** (`lstat` per component). Root symlinkness (`/tmp` itself) is legitimate; a symlink inside the runtime dir is refused.
   - Dot, dot-dot and empty components refused outright before any path is built (a textual root-prefix check passes `/tmp/../etc/svc.sock` — reproduced in T-008).
   - **Credential model** (T-008's answer to peer-UID is NO — Node 22 exposes no such API without a native build, which the no-build rule forbids): the runtime dir is validated as the **primary isolation boundary** — lstat type, owner uid, non-symlink, mode exactly 0700 masked at 0o7777, every rejection branch reachable via injected stats; a 32-byte token published **write-once via `link()`** with a directory fsync (exclusive-create-then-write would expose an empty token to a concurrent first-run); files created with `fchmod` after open plus `fstat` verification so a hostile umask can neither leak the token (0644) nor permanently brick the install (0400); comparison hashes both values and `timingSafeEqual`s the fixed-size digests, so wrong-length and wrong-byte rejections share one code path — no length oracle, no timing branch.
   - **Stale socket — corrected per ISS-041.** Probe-then-unlink is read-then-act: between the probe and the unlink another process can bind the pathname, so the old criterion "a live server's socket is never unlinked" is unsatisfiable as an absolute and is withdrawn. What ships instead: reclamation happens only at the fixed point in the startup order below — i.e. only by the process already holding the singleton port — which serializes all **cooperating** spendbar instances (provable deterministically) but only **narrows** the window against an unrelated or hostile same-UID process. Per ISS-041, the residual must be closed or accepted explicitly: (a) a per-instance socket path published through the write-once allocation, so no pathname is ever reused and nothing is reclaimed; or (b) the residual same-UID denial-of-service is documented as accepted. If (a), an adversarial competing-binder test in the probe/unlink window is required, not only cooperative failure injection. (Open question 5.)
   - **Startup order (fixed by the T-008 handover)**: validate write-once token → validate write-once allocation → acquire port → probe unix socket → reclaim only confirmed-stale → bind socket → serve.
4. **Launcher**: stable user-owned launcher at `~/Library/Application Support/spendbar/launcher` executing recorded absolute `[node, cli.js]` pairs from an allowlisted 0600 registry written only by spendbar. **NO PATH search** (attacker-controlled-binary risk; test with a poisoned PATH). Persistent **installation ID**; the launcher target changes only via explicit `install`/`repair` or a verified same-installation upgrade handoff. A foreground command from a different prefix/version **reports the mismatch and never silently retargets** — and (per ISS-026) the message must name only remedies that exist in the shipped version: it may say "run `spendbar service repair`" only if minimal repair ships in v0.2 (open question 3); otherwise it must direct the user to re-run `service install` from the owning installation.
5. **Minimal durable `service install|start|stop`** + LaunchAgent plist targeting the launcher (no `LimitLoadToSessionType: Aqua` on the service — that key is menubar-view-only). **Stop sequencing (final, round-4)**: persist desired state = stopped → disable relaunch (KeepAlive would otherwise respawn) → request graceful shutdown OVER THE SOCKET → wait to deadline → then boot out the launchd job → remove the socket only under the stale-socket rule above. Ordering matters: unloading first kills the process before it receives the request. `service start` reverses each step after partial failure. **No PID-based control anywhere** (PID reuse) — the adopted design contains no PID in any coordination state at all.
6. **`spendbar refresh`** CLI command (v0.2 phase deliverable): reader-side trigger over the socket; this is the "explicit user refresh" that bypasses T-012's full-tier cap.

## Scope — out

- Full upgrade/downgrade/prefix-change/nvm-removal matrix, `doctor`, `setup` wizard, uninstall ownership → v0.3. v0.3 adds the matrix, **not the mechanism** — the mechanism ships here.
- Menubar view and attach/quit semantics → v0.3.
- Zero-touch upgrade survival is explicitly NOT claimed: an npm upgrade/removal breaks the recorded path until the next foreground invocation of the OWNING installation re-validates + re-records, or the user runs `service repair` (if shipped — open question 3).
- Reboot persistence on SSH-only Macs with no GUI login: LaunchAgents load at user login, so no promise there; documented path is foreground `spendbar service run` (e.g. under tmux). "Headless" = no-menubar operation within a logged-in user session.
- Fast/full tier internals → T-012.
- Defending the loopback port against a hostile OTHER local user → out of scope by design: refuse-to-start with a clear diagnosis is the whole contract there.

## State machines

- **Refresh queue**: queued → coalesced | running → publishing → published | discarded; generation numbers monotonic; publish-if-current is the only publish path inside the service.
- **Service lifecycle**: desired state (installed/started/stopped) vs actual; stop and start are multi-step sequences with per-step failure injection and reversal.
- **Lock ownership (rewritten to the adopted primitive)**: acquire (or adopt the publication listener) → held — exclusion exactly while the listener stays bound → released | **lost** (unrequested close raises the loss witness; publishing is irreversibly disabled or the process terminates; in-flight results are discarded, never published). Locks are single-use: a released or lost lock refuses re-acquire/adopt. There is no "revalidate then continue" state — nothing exists to revalidate.

## Failure modes to test (each a named deterministic test)

- **Stale socket**: a crashed server's orphan pathname is reclaimed only at the startup-order point, only by the port holder; a cooperating live server's socket is never unlinked (deterministic schedules). Under option (a): an adversarial binder occupying the pathname in the probe/unlink window never has its socket deleted. Under option (b): the documented residual behavior is asserted, not hidden.
- **Crashed service**: SIGKILL the holder — the kernel releases the port; a fresh start acquires with no staleness judgement and no reclaimed state. Crash injection at each real publication boundary of the allocation protocol (before-publish, mid-publish, after-link, after-lose, after-adopt) converges to exactly one holder; stranded candidates are counted, left alone, and never adopted.
- **Concurrent refresh races**: wake+timer, manual+full, midnight-crossing, shutdown flush, crash storms, wake storms — coalescing observed; no stale generation ever becomes current.
- **Partial stop/start**: failure injected at every stop/start transition; `start` recovers from any partial `stop`; a stopping service is not respawned by KeepAlive.
- **Two writers racing**: a first-run bootstrap storm of real child processes agrees on ONE port (one holder, the rest blocked); a second `service run` against a live holder authenticates it, reports already-running, exits cleanly and never publishes.
- **Lock loss mid-run**: induced unrequested listener close → loss witness fires, no further publish, in-flight job discarded; the mutant publish path omitting the pre-commit `assertHeld()` fails the suite.
- **Foreign holder**: a foreign or unidentifiable listener on the allocated port → named refuse-to-start error, allocation file byte-identical afterwards; a mutant caller that "recovers" by allocating a second port is caught by that byte-identity assertion.
- **Foreign installation**: mismatch reported, registry unchanged.
- **Hostile umask**: under umasks 022, 0200 and 077 (child-process tests), runtime dir, token and allocation are created at their exact modes via fchmod-after-open + fstat verify; exact-mode validation (masked 0o7777, so setuid/setgid/sticky are caught) rejects everything else.
- **Handoff** (v0.2 exit test): one short-lived CLI command starts indexing, exits; indexing completes with no foreground process — proven on a clean-prefix install.

## Dependencies on gate outcomes

- **T-008 (verdict recorded — no longer pending)**: implement the adopted primitive and credential fallback exactly per `docs/v0.2-prototype-findings.md` §1, §3.4–3.5 and §4, carrying the spike's pinned invariants into production as named regression tests: nothing after `link()` may throw (every hook read into a local before the link; post-link failures reported on the result, never thrown — a throw there strands a permanent allocation naming an unbound port); connection tracking from server **creation** (a connection accepted before identity registration must not wedge `release()` — the reproduced local DoS); injectable deadlines validated at registration (0/negative/NaN/Infinity/Symbol all rejected); single-use locks; `adopt()` validates before mutating state; identity registration is part of BECOMING the holder. `spikes/locking/` is evidence, not a shipping library — production modules are written against those properties, not imported from the spike.
- **T-010 (hard)**: the state machine publishes exclusively through T-010's publication protocol: one self-contained temp file atomically `rename()`d over the target (structural integrity needs no lock — a reader sees the old file or the new one, never a torn one), with a per-source-offset manifest and incomparable-fails-closed dominance rules. Snapshot fsync is deliberately NOT specified here: the findings record process-crash atomicity without power-loss durability for the derived snapshot (losing it costs a recomputation), T-010's earlier text says otherwise, and that conflict is **ISS-030's to settle in T-010** — this ticket takes whatever T-010 decides. Schema-range policy (an older writer refuses to publish on a newer schema) stands.
- T-009 is not a dependency of this ticket (MCP-side only).

## Constraints

No npm lifecycle scripts; no native builds; `usage.py` is frozen and never modified (service is TS-only); `package.json` never carries an author field; no real transcript data, personal paths, or session/rollout identifiers in fixtures — service tests run on synthetic corpora with placeholder paths (e.g. `/Users/testuser`); the packaging content scan enforces this for shipped files.

## Approach notes

Design the state machine around an injectable clock/scheduler from day one or the race tests will be flaky; the plan's quality bar requires deterministic tests, not sleeps. Launchd plist load behavior needs a macOS runner (CI section of the plan) and some paths may only be verifiable via abstraction plus owner-machine runs — record which is which. Carry T-008's dominant defect pattern as a working rule: the spike's recurring failure was fixing a class in one site and not its siblings (seven instances); after any class-level correction here, grep for the RULE ("every file this ticket creates", "every deadline this ticket accepts"), not the symptom, and check every site before reporting.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Clean-prefix install test: `service install` + `service start`, then one short-lived CLI command triggers indexing and exits; a new generation is published with no foreground spendbar process remaining (the v0.2 handoff exit test).
2. Control socket round-trips status/refresh/stop/progress with request IDs; oversized messages rejected; unauthenticated peer rejected via the digest-hashed `timingSafeEqual` token comparison (findings §4); protocol-version mismatch returns a typed error.
3. Socket path: a canonical path over 104 bytes is rejected **before `listen` is ever called** — proven by a test injecting a realpath that pushes a fitting requested path over the limit and asserting `listen` is never reached; dot/dot-dot/empty components refused; a symlink inside the runtime dir refused while a symlinked root (`/tmp`) is accepted; no post-listen check serves as a primary guard. (The uid-keyed path makes long usernames/home paths irrelevant by construction — that replaces the old long-username test matrix.)
4. Stop sequencing: failure injected at each step (persist desired state, disable relaunch, socket shutdown, deadline wait, bootout, socket removal under the stale-socket rule); after any partial failure `service start` restores a working service; a stopped service does not respawn via KeepAlive.
5. Composed single-instance startup drives four cases end-to-end: first run allocates, holds, and registers identity as part of becoming holder; a second start against our own live instance reports already-running, exits cleanly, never publishes; a foreign holder throws the named refuse-to-start error; an unidentifiable holder throws too (indeterminate collapses into neither answer) — with the allocation file **byte-identical** after every refusal. Mutants caught: a caller that continues after "foreign"; one that recovers by allocating a second port; one that skips identity registration.
6. Lock-loss discipline: every publish path calls `assertHeld()` immediately before its atomic commit with no awaits in between — a mutant omitting it MUST fail; induced listener loss → `onLost` terminates the process or irreversibly disables publishing, and a quiet-return handler is rejected; no publish ever lands after an observed loss.
7. Deterministic race tests pass without sleeps-as-synchronization: wake+timer, manual+full, midnight-crossing, shutdown flush, crash storm, wake storm; publish-if-current holds in every schedule (no superseded generation becomes current).
8. Launcher: registry file mode 0600 in 0700 dir; launcher refuses targets not in the allowlisted registry; runs correctly with a poisoned PATH containing a fake `node` (proving no PATH search); foreign-prefix invocation prints the mismatch message — naming only remedies that exist in the shipped version — and changes nothing.
9. No PID-based control: control flows only via the socket plus the write-once token challenge; a codebase search for kill-by-pid control paths comes up empty; no PID, process-start-time, or inode field exists in any coordination state.
10. `spendbar refresh` reaches the running service over the socket and triggers a refresh; with no service running it fails with a clear, typed message.
11. Allocation lifecycle: write-once via `link()`; an adversary binding the allocated port between publication and adoption gets `EADDRINUSE` (continuous reservation — no close-and-rebind gap); the crash matrix converges to one holder in every row; a post-link durability failure is reported, not thrown, and the listener is retained (adversary bind still refused).
12. Modes under hostile umasks: child-process tests across umasks 022, 0200 and 077 prove runtime dir (0700), token and allocation (0600) are created exactly and validated exactly (masked at 0o7777); a wrong mode is refused fail-closed, never repaired in place.

## Risks

The T-008 gate risk is retired — the verdict is recorded and this ticket now implements it. Remaining and new risks: the honest exclusion contract makes `assertHeld`/`onLost` **requirements on this ticket rather than properties of the primitive** — a publish path that skips the guard silently loses the safety property, and the mutant tests are the only defense; the stale-socket residual window (ISS-041) is a real same-UID DoS if option (b) is chosen — it must be documented, not discovered; a machine-wide port means another local user can deny startup (accepted: refuse-to-start, never two writers — but support docs must diagnose it, and a sandbox forbidding loopback binds must read as an environment failure, not "lock held"). Launchd behavior is only partially testable in CI (macOS runner required; some sequences may need owner-machine verification — record which). Race tests become flaky unless the scheduler/clock is injectable from the first commit. The launcher registry is security-sensitive (0600 allowlist, no PATH search); a shortcut here becomes an attacker-controlled-binary execution path. Finally, T-008's history warns that this design's defects recur as a class fixed in one site and not its siblings — budget review time accordingly.

## Open questions

(The former question on the runtime-dir location is resolved by T-008's measurements: `/tmp/spendbar-<uid>`, keyed on uid so the canonical path length is bounded by construction — recorded in the findings doc, no longer open.)
1. Wire framing for the control protocol: the plan fixes properties (request IDs, bounded sizes, version negotiation) but not the encoding (JSON-lines vs length-prefixed). Note the identity-challenge protocol already fixes its own framing (length-framed 32-byte nonce, reply at the challenger's half-close) and is separate from the control protocol.
2. Mechanism for 'disable relaunch' in the stop sequence (plist rewrite of KeepAlive vs launchctl override) and the exact plist keys (RunAtLoad, ThrottleInterval, KeepAlive shape).
3. Whether a minimal `service repair` (adopt) ships in v0.2 — sharpened by ISS-026: whichever way this goes, the mismatch message must name only commands that actually exist in the shipped version.
4. Graceful-shutdown deadline value before bootout (no number in the plan).
5. Stale-socket residual (ISS-041): option (a) per-instance never-reused socket path published through the write-once allocation, or option (b) documented acceptance of the same-UID DoS window. A delegated design decision (not owner-only), but it must be settled explicitly in plan review before the socket code lands — each option's required tests are named in Scope item 3.

## Scope addition (N-008 5a, 2026-08-04)

The control socket carries a **pin-request path**: readers (MCP, CLI cursors) request a pin over the socket; the SERVICE — the sole holder of write authority — validates and executes createPin, returning the pin id or a typed refusal. Readers never construct an authority and never write. This is new surface scoped here because T-013's AC 4 consumes it and nothing else can provide it. Re-plan against N-007/N-008; the preserved plan doc docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md is the base, not a restart.

park.reason:
PARKED after 3 review rounds (reject / reject / reject; 11 + 12 + 9 findings, all valid, none contested). The park reason is a defect in the FILING, at two independent places. Reviewer's own words on round 3: 'The correct disposition is park.'

=== PARK REASON 1 (critical) — the ticket specifies a design the adopted decision forbids. Filed as ISS-084. ===

Base plan section 1 Q5 (docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md:211) DECIDED open question 5 as option (a) LITERALLY: per-process nonce socket path /tmp/spendbar-<uid>/svc-<32 hex>.sock published in endpoint.json, and NO unix-socket pathname is ever unlinked — not by us, not by Node. That decision exists because a probe was measured deleting a RIVAL process's live socket at the same pathname.

The ticket still specifies the design that replaced. Four sites, each verified verbatim against the ticket text this round:
1. Scope item 3 FIXES the socket path: 'Unix-domain socket at /tmp/spendbar-<uid>/svc.sock'. Option (a) requires the nonce path. Direct contradiction.
2. Scope item 3 fixes the startup order and marks it '(fixed by the T-008 handover)': '... acquire port -> PROBE UNIX SOCKET -> RECLAIM ONLY CONFIRMED-STALE -> bind socket -> serve'. Option (a) requires that nothing is ever probed-and-reclaimed.
3. Scope item 5's stop sequence: 'remove the socket only under the stale-socket rule above'. Under option (a) there is no socket removal at all.
4. AC 4 enumerates it as a step requiring failure injection: '... deadline wait, bootout, SOCKET REMOVAL UNDER THE STALE-SOCKET RULE'. An acceptance criterion names a step the adopted design forbids from existing.

Why the delegation does not cover this: the ticket delegates Q5 ('settled explicitly in plan review before the socket code lands'), so plan review WAS authorized to choose (a) over (b). But a delegation to pick between two options is not authority to rewrite an acceptance criterion or to overturn text the ticket itself marks as fixed by a DIFFERENT gate (T-008). Sites 1 and 2 are presented as fixed, not as consequences of Q5; site 4 is an AC. Amending those is the owner's call.

This is a defect I should have caught myself and did not: I re-planned against the base DOCUMENT for three revisions and never re-read the TICKET's scope, startup order, failure matrix and AC 4 against the Q5 decision.

=== PARK REASON 2 (major) — AC 10 is not satisfiable as written. Filed as ISS-085. ===

AC 10: 'spendbar refresh reaches the running service over the socket and TRIGGERS A REFRESH'. The base plan's accepted reduction is that T-011 alone indexes once (every generation carries sourceVersion = {}, so no later candidate can dominate). The honest post-bootstrap behaviour is to decline at ADMISSION, before spawning ccusage — spending 60-120s on a run known in advance to be incapable of publishing is worse than declining, and it makes a healthy service indistinguishable from a broken one. So after the bootstrap publish no refresh is triggered.

Two readings are defensible and they lead to different tickets: (a) AC 10 means 'reaches the service and gets a truthful typed answer' -> amend it to say so explicitly and T-011 proceeds; (b) AC 10 means 'a refresh executes on every invocation' -> not satisfiable in v0.2, and T-011 holds on ISS-082 then ISS-081. Revision 2 assumed (a) silently and that was wrong; revision 3 identified the contradiction in its own park-assessment section and then concluded NOT parked anyway, which is worse than missing it.

=== WHAT IS *NOT* THE PARK REASON ===

The other 7 findings of round 3 are ordinary review findings that revision would address. They matter to whoever unparks, so: (3) manifest retention proves protection from GC, NOT readability — my proposed pin reduction was the available-vs-consumed substitution class again, and ISS-083 has been CORRECTED because I had written that false claim into it; (4) refreshTier is validated by requireString alone (store.ts:1075), so a usable generation with sourceVersion:{} and a non-bootstrap marker defeats the bootstrap-only admission check and reaches SnapshotNotDominatingError('equal') — my unreachability proof was not universal; (5) 'no production caller reaches the replacement seam' repeats the absence-proof defect the base ALREADY rejected at its lines 981-988 for the recording publisher, and needs a nominal runtime brand instead (found by my own self-audit before the review returned); (6) the closed refresh outcome type omits cancelled / superseded-coalesced / authority-lost, which AC 6 and shutdown require to stay distinct; (7) control peers share ONE token so 'per client' has no authenticated identity, and an in-memory idempotency map loses across restart; (8) one execution queue cannot both be one queue and let pin mutations overtake a 60-120s ccusage phase — needs a separate short store-mutation arbiter; (9) the retry exclusion must be conditional on the failed attempt persisting no trace.

=== UNPARK ORDER ===

1. ISS-084 — owner amends the ticket's four Q5 sites. Text-only; nothing blocks it.
2. ISS-085 — owner rules on what AC 10 means.
3. Then the round-3 findings are ordinary re-plan work, EXCEPT that findings 3 and 4 depend on ISS-083 (store-owned validate-and-create-pin) and on ISS-082 respectively.

=== PRESERVED ===

docs/t011-replan-n007-n008-rev3.md (241 lines) — the revision-3 delta plan: the per-amendment supersession map, the two base-document contradictions found and corrected (version-bound vs Q5; the probe cache absent from the coordination inventory), the contributing-set definition for ccusageInvokedAt, and the correction tables for revisions 1 and 2. .story/sessions/ is gitignored, so this copy is the only one that survives. The 1234-line base remains at docs/t011-headless-service-plan.md.

Issues filed or corrected this round: ISS-083 (created, then CORRECTED — its original reduction was unsound), ISS-084 (critical, the park reason), ISS-085 (high), ISS-082 (amended to record that it blocks a T-011 scope item directly, which I had denied).
